![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The function `IsKDNNEnabled()` is called here but is not declared or defined anywhere in this pull request or the standard TensorFlow codebase. This will result in a compilation failure when building with KDNN enabled. Please define `IsKDNNEnabled()` or replace it with the appropriate compile-time macro check.

![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The index `a_indices(i, lhs_index_a)` is used directly to access and increment elements in `row_counts` without any bounds checking. Since sparse tensor indices are user-provided, an out-of-bounds index can lead to arbitrary memory corruption or a segmentation fault. Add defensive bounds checks to ensure `a_indices(i, lhs_index_a)` is within `[0, lhs_left)` before accessing `row_counts`.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The current implementation performs the comparison `x == 0` twice and creates two separate `ones_like` tensors (`ones_like(pi_x)` and `ones_like(x)`), which are identical in shape and dtype. We can optimize this by computing the condition and the `ones` tensor once and reusing them. This reduces redundant operations and memory usage in the generated graph.

```suggestion
    cond = x == 0
    ones = array_ops.ones_like(x)
    safe_pi_x = array_ops.where_v2(cond, ones, pi_x)
    return array_ops.where_v2(
        cond, ones, math_ops.sin(safe_pi_x) / safe_pi_x
    )
```

</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Linker version scripts standardly use C-style comments (`/* ... */`). Using `#` for comments is non-standard and can cause syntax errors with some linkers (such as older versions of GNU `ld` or certain toolchains) that do not preprocess the version script. Please use C-style comments instead.

```
    /* Do not re-export bundled hwloc. Its objects also land in other DSOs
       (e.g. _xla_ops.so); hiding at compile time is the complete fix, this
       is extra protection for libtensorflow_framework.so (tensorflow#125854). */
```

TensorFlow version scripts already use `#` comments (e.g. `tensorflow/c/version_script.lds`, and this file did before the ROCm `global: *;` rewrite). GNU ld accepted this script as-is. I’ll keep `#` for consistency with the rest of the tree.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When `window_length` is 1 dynamically, `n` becomes 0, which leads to a division by zero (`count / n`) and results in `NaN` values in `cos_arg`. Since `cos_arg` is defined outside `_compute_window`, it is evaluated even when `window_length` is 1 (e.g., in eager mode or during graph construction/execution of the conditional's inputs).

To prevent this division by zero, we should define `n`, `count`, and `cos_arg` inside `_compute_window`, so they are only evaluated when `window_length > 1`.

```python
    def _compute_window():
      n = math_ops.cast(window_length + periodic * even - 1, dtype=dtype)
      count = math_ops.cast(math_ops.range(window_length), dtype)
      cos_arg = constant_op.constant(2 * np.pi, dtype=dtype) * count / n
      return math_ops.cast(
          0.42 - 0.5 * math_ops.cos(cos_arg) + 0.08 * math_ops.cos(2 * cos_arg),
          dtype=dtype)
```

</details>

+@tf_export('signal.blackman_window')
+@dispatch.add_dispatch_support
+def blackman_window(window_length, periodic=True, dtype=dtypes.float32,
+                    name=None):
+  """Generate a [Blackman][blackman] window.
+
+  Args:
+    window_length: A scalar `Tensor` indicating the window length to generate.
+    periodic: A bool `Tensor` indicating whether to generate a periodic or
+      symmetric window. Periodic windows are typically used for spectral
+      analysis while symmetric windows are typically used for digital
+      filter design.
+    dtype: The data type to produce. Must be a floating point type.
+    name: An optional name for the operation.
+
+  Returns:
+    A `Tensor` of shape `[window_length]` of type `dtype`.
+
+  Raises:
+    ValueError: If `dtype` is not a floating point type.
+
+  [blackman]:
+    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Window_function#Blackman_window
+  """
+  if not dtype.is_floating:
+    raise ValueError('dtype must be a floating point type. Found %s' % dtype)
+
+  with ops.name_scope(name, 'blackman_window', [window_length, periodic]):
+    window_length = ops.convert_to_tensor(window_length, dtype=dtypes.int32,
+                                          name='window_length')
+    window_length.shape.assert_has_rank(0)
+    window_length_const = tensor_util.constant_value(window_length)
+    if window_length_const == 1:
+      return array_ops.ones([1], dtype=dtype)
+    periodic = math_ops.cast(
+        ops.convert_to_tensor(periodic, dtype=dtypes.bool, name='periodic'),
+        dtypes.int32)
+    periodic.shape.assert_has_rank(0)
+    even = 1 - math_ops.mod(window_length, 2)
+
+    n = math_ops.cast(window_length + periodic * even - 1, dtype=dtype)
+    count = math_ops.cast(math_ops.range(window_length), dtype)
+    cos_arg = constant_op.constant(2 * np.pi, dtype=dtype) * count / n
+
+    def _compute_window():
+      return math_ops.cast(
+          0.42 - 0.5 * math_ops.cos(cos_arg) + 0.08 * math_ops.cos(2 * cos_arg),
+          dtype=dtype)
